FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A33
A sign’s shape, color, symbols and wording help identify whether it communicates rules, hazards, directions, locations or services. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A33
Warning signs usually have a diamond shape with a yellow background and black words or symbols. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A33
Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing warnings use fluorescent yellow. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A33
A warning sign announces possible danger or a special road situation and may require slowing or preparing to stop. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A33
Before a rail crossing, a round yellow sign with an X and black RR letters warns drivers to slow, look, listen and prepare to stop for an approaching train. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A33
A white X-shaped crossbuck marked Railroad Crossing stands at the highway-rail intersection. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A33
The clear portion of the crossbuck paragraph requires stopping behind the stop line when a train or rail vehicle approaches. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A34
A multiple-track sign warns that another track and another train may be present. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A34
Always check for additional tracks and trains because some multiple-track crossings lack the number-of-tracks sign and some crossings have no lights. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A34
Alternately flashing rail-crossing lights require a stop. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A34
Never drive around a lowered rail-crossing gate. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A34
Where a rail-crossing bell or horn sounds, do not cross until the warning sound stops. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A34
The railroad emergency-notification sign provides a dispatch phone number for reporting crossing, track or train problems. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A34
The emergency-notification number is generally on a blue sign at or near the crossing. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A34
The same sign’s DOT number identifies the crossing location for emergency crews and railroad staff. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A34
Give the crossing’s DOT identifier when reporting trouble so dispatch can identify it and warn or slow approaching trains. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A34
Work-zone signs are generally orange with black markings and have diamond or rectangular shapes. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A34
Work-zone warnings may announce workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment or changing road surfaces. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A34
Obey a work-zone controller’s signs or flags directing travel, slowing or stopping. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A34
Work-zone drums, cones, panels and barricades guide traffic away from hazardous or closed areas. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A34
Temporary work-zone signals may be used, and a driver stopping there must stop at a white line when one is present. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A34
In a work zone, slow down, expect sudden stops and avoid following too closely. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A34
Speeding fines in a work zone may be doubled. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A35
Regulatory signs communicate laws for direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and other situations that drivers must obey. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A35
Regulatory signs are white with black, red or green markings and may be square, rectangular or specially shaped. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A35
A red circle and slash over a regulatory symbol prohibit the action represented. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A35
Black-and-white speed signs state the maximum permitted speed or a required minimum. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R28 | anchor: A35
Use the posted maximum only in ideal conditions and reduce speed for slippery roads, precipitation, ice or limited visibility. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R29 | anchor: A35
On a road with a minimum speed, use another road if that posted minimum is too fast for you. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R30 | anchor: A35
A stop sign is red with white lettering and has 8 sides. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R31 | anchor: A35
At a stop sign, stop behind an existing stop line or crosswalk, or before the sign when neither is present, then check every direction and yield. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R32 | anchor: A35
A yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle with red lettering. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R33 | anchor: A35
A yield sign requires slowing and giving priority to traffic in the intersection or road being entered. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R34 | anchor: A35
On a one-way street, travel only in the arrow’s direction and never turn or drive against it. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R35 | anchor: A35
No-passing signs and pavement markings identify passing-zone beginnings and endings and places where passing is prohibited. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R36 | anchor: A35
Passing-zone placement considers visible distance and hidden hazards such as hills, curves, intersections and driveways. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec09-R37 | anchor: A35
Even where passing is permitted, pass only when safe in the actual road and traffic conditions. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0035]
